title: Training Overparametrized Neural Networks in Sublinear Time

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to reduce the per-iteration cost of second-order (Gauss-Newton) training for overparameterized deep neural networks from linear to sublinear in network size while maintaining fast convergence rates, addressing scalability bottlenecks in hyperparameterized DNN training. Paper [4] ("Training Overparametrized Neural Networks in Sublinear Time") shares the same objective of reducing computational costs in training overparameterized neural networks, specifically targeting sublinear time complexity. Paper [11] ("Training Multi-Layer Over-Parametrized Neural Network in Subquadratic Time") also addresses the scalability bottleneck in training overparameterized networks, albeit with subquadratic rather than sublinear time complexity. Both papers aim to improve scalability in DNN training, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The contribution introduces a novel perspective of viewing DNNs as binary search trees, leveraging activation sparsity to update only a subset of tree paths, combined with sketch maintenance, sublinear iterative regression solvers, and implicit weight maintenance. Paper [27] ("Efficient SGD Neural Network Training via Sublinear Activated Neuron Identification") uses a similar mechanism of identifying activated neurons in sublinear time for efficient training, leveraging sparsity in activation patterns. Paper [26] ("Efficient Second Order Online Learning by Sketching") employs sketching techniques for efficient second-order optimization, which aligns with the contribution's use of sketch maintenance and sublinear iterative regression solvers. Paper [16] ("Revisiting Sub-sampled Newton Methods") and Paper [17] ("RSN: Randomized Subspace Newton") both use randomized sketching and sub-sampled Newton methods for efficient second-order optimization, which overlaps with the contribution's mechanism at the primitive level. Thus, the mechanism is covered.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates its method theoretically, comparing computational per-iteration costs and convergence rates against prior work (e.g., Brand et al. 2021). Paper [4] ("Training Overparametrized Neural Networks in Sublinear Time") uses a similar evaluation design, comparing theoretical computational costs and convergence rates for sublinear training methods. Paper [11] ("Training Multi-Layer Over-Parametrized Neural Network in Subquadratic Time") also evaluates theoretical computational costs and convergence rates for overparameterized networks. Both papers use the same evaluation design (theoretical analysis of computational complexity and convergence rates), making the evaluation covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of deep learning optimization theory and neural network training algorithm complexity. Paper [4] ("Training Overparametrized Neural Networks in Sublinear Time") and Paper [11] ("Training Multi-Layer Over-Parametrized Neural Network in Subquadratic Time") both address the same domain of deep learning optimization theory and neural network training complexity. Paper [6] ("Review of second-order optimization techniques in artificial neural networks backpropagation") also operates in the same domain, focusing on second-order optimization techniques for neural networks. Thus, the domain is covered.

### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to provide a data structure that supports the core step of dynamically retrieving weights satisfying an inner product threshold (≥τ) in sublinear query time relative to \(m\). This aligns with the general problem of efficient Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS). Papers [1], [9], [12], [19], and [21] all address MIPS, with [9] and [19] specifically focusing on sublinear time solutions. For example, [9] introduces asymmetric locality-sensitive hashing (ALSH) for sublinear MIPS, and [19] improves upon ALSH for MIPS. These papers share the same high-level objective of enabling efficient inner product-based retrieval, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a data structure for solving Dynamic Sensitive Weight Searching (DSWS) with update time \(\tilde{O}(nd)\) and query time \(\tilde{O}(K_q)\), where \(K_q\) is the number of neurons satisfying \(\langle w_j, x_i \rangle \geq \tau\), leveraging sparsity to ensure \(|K_q| \leq m^{0.76}\). This mechanism is a specific instantiation of efficient data structures for inner product search. Papers [1], [9], [12], and [19] propose data structures for MIPS, including hashing-based and tree-based approaches. For example, [9] uses asymmetric transformations to convert MIPS into a nearest neighbor search problem, while [19] introduces a different transformation for improved efficiency. Although the specific sparsity guarantee (\(|K_q| \leq m^{0.76}\)) is new, the underlying primitive of designing efficient data structures for inner product search is covered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation facet involves theoretical analysis of query time (\(\tilde{O}(m^{0.76})\)), total time (\(\tilde{O}(n \cdot m^{0.76})\)), and space complexity (\(O(mn + nd + md)\)). Papers [9], [12], and [19] also evaluate MIPS data structures using theoretical guarantees on query time, preprocessing time, and space complexity. For instance, [9] provides sublinear time guarantees for MIPS using ALSH, and [19] analyzes the efficiency of their improved ALSH variant. The evaluation design — theoretical analysis of time and space complexity — is standard in this area and covered by these prior works.

### Domain
The domain of the contribution is algorithms and data structures for neural network training, specifically focusing on efficient weight retrieval during training. Papers [5], [8], and [22] address sparsity and efficiency in neural network training, while papers [1], [9], [12], and [19] focus on MIPS, which is a general algorithmic problem applicable across domains, including neural networks. Since MIPS is a well-established problem in the broader domain of algorithms and data structures, and neural network training is a specific application within this domain, the domain is covered.
